Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Underwriting Officer; Elena Petrov, Chief Investment Officer; Mark Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; Tara Nguyen, Chief Claims Officer; and Kevin Walsh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust share repurchase activity, premium growth momentum with clear guidance ahead, solid net written premiums expansion across lines of business, vibrant new business production, a fortified capital position with elevated statutory surplus levels, manageable catastrophe losses relative to gross written premiums, favorable expense ratio trends amid commission and operating efficiencies, and reliable reinsurance recoveries both realized and anticipated. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Maria Gonzalez, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included accelerated share repurchases, premium growth outperformance, net written premium gains by segment, new business surges, capital strength, controlled catastrophe impacts, expense discipline, and reinsurance support.

Let me expand on these starting with our share repurchase activity, which has been a key pillar of our disciplined capital allocation framework this year. In the insurance industry, we prioritize returning excess capital to shareholders when we generate strong underwriting profitability, favorable reserve development, and robust investment income from our float—all while maintaining robust statutory capital positions across our property & casualty, life & annuity, and specialty lines portfolios.

In Q3, we executed $750 million in share repurchases, acquiring approximately 6.2 million shares at an average price of $121 per share. This brings our year-to-date total to $2.4 billion, representing about 4.1% of our shares outstanding at the beginning of the year. We've made meaningful progress against our $5 billion share repurchase authorization announced in February, with roughly $2.6 billion remaining as of quarter-end. For context, this pace is up 35% from the $1.8 billion we repurchased in the first nine months of 2023, reflecting our confidence in the sustainability of our mid-teens return on equity trajectory.

These buybacks are highly accretive to earnings per share—adding an estimated 2.8% to our adjusted operating EPS for the quarter alone, net of any dilution from our employee share plans. On a trailing 12-month basis, repurchases have contributed over 5% to EPS growth, helping offset some of the pricing pressure we're seeing in select personal auto lines amid softening commercial combined ratios industry-wide.

Diving into the technical execution, we've leaned heavily on our accelerated share repurchase program with a major investment bank counterparty, which allowed us to opportunistically repurchase blocks at a 2-3% discount to VWAP during periods of market volatility tied to Fed rate cut expectations. We've also employed 10b5-1 trading plans to systematically buy during off-hours and collar structures to cap our average cost basis below $118 per share in Q3. This disciplined approach mirrors what we've seen from peers like Travelers and Chubb, who have similarly ramped up ASR usage to minimize market impact and execution risk. Importantly, our repurchase yield—total spend divided by average market cap—stood at 3.2% YTD, competitive with our 2.8% dividend yield and well above the S&P 500 insurance index average of 2.1%.

Regionally, our activity has been fueled by divergent performance across our geographies. In the US, which accounts for 62% of our $18.2 billion in Q3 gross written premiums, we've seen exceptional capital generation from our commercial P&C book. Catastrophe losses were just 2.5 points on the combined ratio—our best Q3 since 2019—thanks to proactive rate actions averaging 8.2% in middle market E&S lines and favorable prior-year development of $285 million. This freed up approximately $1.1 billion in deployable capital post-dividend, with 65% directed to buybacks. Contrast that with Europe, where our life & health segment faced headwinds from lower lapses and persistent morbidity trends in group protection products, limiting local repurchases to just $150 million equivalent. In Asia-Pacific, strong growth in our direct-to-consumer term life offerings—up 14% YoY—combined with higher reinvestment yields from JGBs amid Bank of Japan normalization, supported $200 million in activity, though we're pacing it to preserve solvency margins above 200% under local regs.

Strategically, share repurchases remain a core tool for enhancing shareholder value in this capital-rich environment. With interest rates stabilizing around the 4.25-4.50% Fed funds range, our fixed income portfolio is yielding 4.8%—up 60 bps YoY—bolstering net investment income to $1.2 billion in Q3. This, paired with a consolidated accident year ex-cat combined ratio of 92.4%, has driven free cash flow conversion above 110% of net income. We're trading at 1.4x tangible book value, a 15% discount to our peer group median (think Progressive at 2.2x and Berkshire's insurance ops implicitly higher), signaling we're undervalued relative to our embedded value in long-tail liabilities and our 15-year track record of 95%+ reserve adequacy.

Looking ahead, we expect to deploy another $800 million to $1 billion in Q4, contingent on maintaining our RBC ratio above 550%—currently at 612%—and monitoring for any escalation in secondary perils like California wildfires, which we've already priced for with 12% rate hikes in homeowners. This isn't just financial engineering; it's a vote of confidence in our ability to navigate a soft cycle in personal lines while growing specialty and reinsurance amid hardening terms post-Hurricane Helene analogs. Compared to Munich Re's more conservative stance or AIG's pivot to divestitures, our buyback program underscores our fortress balance sheet and focus on total shareholder return, targeting 10-12% TSR through the cycle.

Turning now to premium growth guidance, another key metric underscoring our disciplined pricing strategy, robust retention, and expanding new business pipeline amid a dynamic market environment. For the full year 2024, we now expect written premium growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year, up slightly from our prior guide of 8% to 10%. This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum in our core property & casualty lines, where we've realized mid-single-digit rate increases across most books of business, complemented by a 92% policy retention rate—our highest in five years. In Q3 alone, we delivered 10.2% written premium growth, driven by 7% organic expansion and 3.2% from our recent tuck-in acquisition of Midwest Specialty Risk Partners, which bolsters our excess & surplus lines.

Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we guide to written premium growth of 6% to 8%, moderating from Q3 due to anticipated seasonal normalization in personal lines and some pull-forward of new business ahead of year-end rate filings. Quarter-over-quarter, this implies a sequential uptick from Q3's earned premium pace, as we lap easier comps from last year's California wildfire cats.

For fiscal year 2025, our initial guidance calls for written premium growth of 10% to 12%, positioning us at the high end of industry consensus. This outlook assumes continued pricing discipline—targeting 4% to 6% net rate adequacy across segments—stable catastrophe frequency aligned with RMS 20-year modeled averages, and low-teens new business growth.

By segment: Personal Lines, 45% of premiums, expect 8% to 10% growth in 2025, led by homeowners up 12% benefiting from 5.5% rate hikes approved in Florida and Texas amid elevated rebuild costs, and personal auto 6% to 8%. Our Snapshot telematics program, now with 4.2 million enrolled policyholders—rivaling Progressive's scale—continues to deliver 15% better loss ratios through usage-based pricing, driving 25% YoY growth in this cohort.

Commercial Lines, 35% of premiums: 11% to 13% growth, fueled by mid-market workers' comp and general liability, where we've maintained 95%+ retention via account-based underwriting. E&S lines, our fastest grower at 18% in Q3, will accelerate with new capacity in cyber and directors & officers amid hardening markets.

Specialty & Reinsurance, 20% of premiums: 12% to 14% expansion, including parametric products for climate resilience—a $500 million book growing 30% YoY—and our quota share reinsurance renewals at attractive terms, similar to those negotiated by peers like RenaissanceRe.

Regionally: North America, 75% of premiums, core driver at 11% growth in 2025, with U.S. commercial P&C leading on 6% rate gains despite moderating inflation pressures on auto physical damage claims now trending at 3% YoY vs. 8% peak. Canada benefits from our expanded affinity partnerships with major banks.

EMEA, 15%: 9% growth, tempered by UK regulatory scrutiny on motor premiums but offset by 15% expansion in continental Europe D&O following Munich Re's cat bond issuances signaling capacity return.

APAC, 10%: Highest growth at 14%, with India and Australia microinsurance scaling via digital distribution—we've digitized 70% of new business submissions using our AI-powered ZenithEdge platform—capturing share in a market growing at 12% per IRDAI data.

This guidance embeds our commitment to mid-90s combined ratios through technical pricing, where we've deployed machine learning models to refine risk selection, reducing attritional loss ratios by 150 basis points YoY. Inflation remains a watch item—claims severity up 4% in property—but our proactive advocacy in NAIC rate adequacy hearings ensures we stay ahead.

Strategically, we're allocating $250 million in 2025 capex to tech initiatives: expanding generative AI for claims triage (piloted in auto, targeting 20% faster cycle times) and launching ESG-linked products like flood coverage bundled with carbon offset riders, tapping a $10 billion addressable market per McKinsey estimates. M&A remains opportunistic; post-Midwest, we're eyeing $1 billion in deployable capital for high-return E&S platforms.

Finally, risks to the guide include above-norm cat activity—we've stress-tested for a 1-in-100 APAC typhoon at neutral EPS impact—and softening personal auto competition from Lemonade's direct-to-consumer push. Upside levers: further telematics penetration and cyber rate momentum. We remain confident in delivering top-quartile growth while protecting margins.

Next, our net written premiums, or NWP, performance, which came in at $14.2 billion for the quarter, reflecting a robust 11.8% year-over-year growth. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit NWP expansion, driven by a combination of earned rate increases averaging 8.2% across the book, improved retention rates of 89.5%—up 110 basis points from last year—and strong new business flow, particularly in high-margin segments. Excluding the impact of our recent acquisition of Midwest Specialty Partners, organic NWP growth was still an impressive 9.4%.

Personal Lines led with 13.2% growth to $6.8 billion, outpacing the industry average of around 10% as reported by AM Best for large P&C writers. Auto up 14.5% to $4.2 billion, fueled by 9.1% earned rate increase amid persistent auto inflation—repair costs still running 15-20% above pre-pandemic levels per CCC Intelligent Solutions data—and our Snapshot telematics program now covering 2.8 million policies. Retention here hit 91.2%, thanks to usage-based insurance pricing refinements using machine learning that segment risks 25% more accurately than legacy systems. New business grew 18%, capturing share against Progressive with millennials via app-integrated rewards.

Homeowners and other personal: +11.1% to $2.6 billion. Rate actions of 7.8% more than offset mild cat uptick from Hurricane Idalia. Exposure management capped wind growth at 4% in Florida and Texas, aligning with hardening reinsurance. Digital quoting boosted conversions by 22%, premium per risk up 6%. U.S. personal grew 14.1%, UK 8%.

Commercial Lines: +10.1% to $5.1 billion, benefiting from market-wide capacity discipline post-2022's $165 billion global cat losses per Swiss Re sigma. Workers' comp +12.3% to $1.9 billion, 8.5% rates reflecting medical inflation and return-to-office. AI underwriting with Verisk ISO improved loss predictability 15%, new business up 16%. General liability/umbrella +9.2% to $1.8 billion, tempered by social inflation but 7.9% hikes. Property +8.7% to $1.4 billion, 9.4% increases in high-cat zones, RMS v17.1 modeling cut losses 12%. Europe commercial 11.5%, APAC 7% via Ping An JV.

Specialty Lines: +12.9% to $2.3 billion, now 16% of total NWP. D&O +15.4% to $900 million, +6.2% rates from SEC/ESG risks, sidecar with Apollo recycled $400 million. Cyber +18.2% to $700 million, silent exclusions and parametric via CyberGuard amid 42% ransomware rise per Cyence. Other specialty +9.8% to $700 million from supply chain marine. Latin America 14% via Bermuda.

This profile underscores disciplined growth prioritizing ROAC above 15%, Personal Auto at 18.2%, Cyber 22.1%. Cloud pricing engine processes 1.2 million quotes daily at 95% STP, Guidewire partnerships. Reinsurance ceded flat at 22.5%. Q4 NWP 10-12%, upside from CA auto rates, specialty. Risks: rate compression, UBI privacy.

On new business production volume, a leading indicator of top-line momentum: $2.8 billion in new annualized premium equivalent, 18% YoY increase from $2.37 billion in Q2 2023. Policy count: 285,000 new policies, up 22% from 234,000, shifting to higher-premium products.

Life and Health, 62% at $1.74 billion, 21% growth. Universal life +28% to $850 million APE via Zenith FlexLife with income riders, low 4.2% lapses. Group health $520 million +15% from wellness/wearables. Term $370 million, jumbo HNW digital.

P&C 38% at $1.06 billion, 13% growth. Commercial P&C $480 million +16%, telematics with Geotab 15,000 policies, 25% better ratios. Personal $410 million, homeowners +12% post-wildfires, auto +10% ZenithDrive 45-second binds, 18% millennial share. Cyber +45% $170 million post-Change Healthcare.

North America 52% $1.46 billion +20%, hardening rates. EMEA 28% $784 million +14%, UK motor share via comparisons, Barclays bancass. APAC 20% $560 million +22%, India Jio 85,000 micro, China Ping An +30%.

UnderwriteAI live 85%, ML on 1.2B points slashes reviews 40%, VNB margins 22% +150bps. Embedded via Stripe/Shopify $120 million, digital 41% volume, 28% conversions Salesforce Einstein.

Focused on profitable growth, mid-teens APE CAGR to 2026, de-emphasized single-premium annuities -10%, PVNBP +19% $4.1B. Risks: geopol APAC, softening P&C. VNB +11% $320 million.

Our capital position and statutory surplus levels remain a cornerstone of financial strength. Consolidated statutory surplus $16.8 billion, +11% YoY, +4% sequential. Top quartile vs. Travelers/Chubb per NAIC. Driven by $1.2 billion operating earnings, 92 COR P&C, $450 million NII at 4.8% fixed yields.

RBC 512% consolidated, >450% target, up from 485% YE23. P&C 528%, L&A 495%. A+ AM Best, AA- S&P.

Organic surplus +7% ex-$800 million gains from bond trades at 5.2% yields. Ex-cat LR -250bps to 58%, mid-single rates commercial.

Cats $650 million pre-tax Helene/windstorms, net 15% surplus via 40% quota share Swiss Re/Munich, saved $300 million.

U.S. 65% $10.9 billion +12%, E&S +18%. Europe €3.2B +9%, Solvency II 220%, motor/cyber 88 COR. APAC $2.5B +6%, bancass DBS term life.

Cat bond $1.5B Hurricane Vertex Re 7.5% cost, -25 RBC points. LC efficiency $400 million freed 2%. ORSA climate TCFD tailwind 10-15 points.

Returned $900 million dividends 2.8% yield, $500 million buyback 4M shares $185 avg. Post-$2.2B Midwest M&A +5 RBC, $150M synergies Guidewire. Excess $3.5B for cyber/parametric 15-20% ROE.

Rock-solid vs. auto inflation 6% YoY Mitchell, geopol marine. Surplus growth >8% annual, 10-12% EPS.

Total catastrophe losses net $1.47 billion, 9.2% of $16.0 billion GWP, vs. $892 million 5.8% Q3'23, +65%. TTM $3.82 billion 7.1% GWP, up from 4.9%. Ex-NAT CAT $1.12 billion peak.

U.S. 62% $912 million 6.1% GWP, Idalia $685 million HO/commercial/auto, FL AAL 2.5x avg, CA fires $147 million FAIR.

APAC 12% $176 million Saola HK/China SME flood.

ROW 5% $72 million Aus fires/Turkey quakes.

$423 million recoveries 1:250 tower Lloyd's/Swiss Re, ceded 29%, 2 reinstatements $18 million.

180bps above RMS v18.1/AIR central, IPCC AR6. Freq 6 events, severity +22% Atlantic NOAA.

Earnings: +820bps AY LR to 68%, COR 98.4% ex-cat vs 92.1% incl, EPS -$0.87 14%.

Reshaping: FL HO 18% rates/15% deduct/22% flood, non-renew 8% coastal. Cat bond $300M parametric, sidecar PartnerRe CA fire, net ret -12%.

ZenithCat AI Maxar/ClimateAi +15% reserves, parametric Aus. Diversify US prop cat 28%->24% GWP, casualty/cyber +11%. Intl APAC cap 10%.

U.S. SE firm 14% OIR, 20% contraction Verisk. Europe EIOPA flood, Asia infra.

FY23 cat $4.1-4.4B 6.5-7.0% GWP, Q4 La Niña. 2024 normalize sub-6%.

Expense ratio 27.2%, -130bps YoY from 28.5%, -40bps seq from Q2 27.6%. Best since Q1'21 pre-inflation. YTD 27.8% beat 28.0-28.5% guide, vs. Progressive 28.9%/Travelers 29.4% S&P.

Commissions 42% base, 11.5% EP - from 12.3%, -7% YoY $1.42B. Ind agents 38% new vs 45%, DTC 32% personal $45B book SecureDirect, conversions +15% JD Power. Bancass Chase/WF $250M sub-5%. U.S. DTC dom $30B personal. Europe IDD cap 10%, UK/Ger 13.2% commercial. APAC WeChat/telco -4%.

Ops 15.7% EP flat YoY, abs +3% $2.18B <9% EP growth. Headcount +1.5% 18,500 data/claims focus.

Tech $450M YTD RPA/gen AI 20% back-office cut '25. AI triage Guidewire PolicyCenter 65% auto <$10k STP, LAE -12%. Tech/prem 4.2% vs ind 5.1% NAIC.

Marketing +5% $380M SecureHome 360 bundle telematics, +18% bundles 89% ret +22% LTV, offset AWS -8% vendors.

Efficient Growth: digital/AI/mix sub-27% LT, 50bps annual tech, NLP uw CA -40% manual. Q4 27.0-27.5%, FY24 27.7%, '25 26.5-27.0% DTC 40%. Risks rates/inv off, telem privacy, $2.5B cash.

Proves expense discipline superior returns <95% COR AM Best.

Finally, reinsurance recoveries: Q3 $1.2 billion received +45% from $825M Q3'23, YTD $3.4B 72% gross ult cats. Expected +$1.8B next 12mo, $1.1B Q4. 95% realization vs ind 88% AM Best.

Helene/Milton $2.8B gross $850M rec $650M exp, 40% QS Swiss/Munich.

CA fires YTD $450M rec $300M exp Renaissance swap. Europe Ciarán $120M Lloyd's arb.

AI Guidewire/RMS billing -35% 78 days, disputes <2%. Divers trad 60%/cat bond 20% TowerCo $500M/ILS 20% Atlas Storm Twelve, Jan1 -5% cost vol commit 12% harden.

Exp pipeline no loss worsen, reinst $400M '25 season. Net cat LR 28% vs 35%, +220bps 92.4% COR.

Review APAC index, coll QS Korean Re Solv II/ORSA. Mid-90s COR 8-10% EP CAGR.

$4.5-5.0B FY recoveries, liq $15B A+ intact.

Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.2 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with RBC ratio at 612%. Our expense ratio also improved to 27.2%.

Raj Singh: Thank you, Maria. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C and specialty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered underwriting platforms and dynamic pricing strategies that incorporate telematics and machine learning for better segmentation.

Elena Petrov: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income yielding 4.8% and selective extensions in investment-grade corporates.

Tara Nguyen: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI triage for auto claims achieving straight-through processing on 65% of low-value cases. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times—down 35% on average—and improved claims resolution rates.

Kevin Walsh: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new ZenithEdge and UnderwriteAI platforms are expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings, with generative AI pilots targeting 20% faster cycle times and cloud migrations boosting straight-through processing to 95%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the share repurchase acceleration and how it fits into your broader capital deployment?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. As Maria detailed, our $750 million Q3 execution and YTD $2.4 billion reflect confidence in our mid-teens ROE sustainability and undervaluation at 1.4x TBV. We'll deploy $800 million to $1 billion more in Q4, prioritizing buybacks alongside dividends while keeping RBC above 550%, balancing growth opportunities in E&S and cyber.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jennifer Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Kim: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Jennifer. Cats at 9.2% GWP this quarter were elevated due to Idalia, Helene analogs, and storms, but net of $1.2 billion recoveries, impact was contained to 28% cat LR. Our reshaping—18% FL rates, cat bonds, AI modeling—positions us for sub-6% long-term, with FY budget 6.5-7.0%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like IDD revisions and NAIC updates on your underwriting strategy?

Raj Singh: Good morning, Alex. Regulatory scrutiny in UK/EU on motor/flood caps commissions but we've optimized mix to DTC/bancass, maintaining discipline. NAIC ORSA climate overlays actually provide RBC tailwinds via better modeling. We're adapting with ESG products and micro-location selection, targeting 4-6% rate adequacy.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platforms like ZenithCat AI and UnderwriteAI?

Kevin Walsh: Good morning, Laura. These platforms are transformative: ZenithCat integrates satellite/climate data for 15% better reserves and dynamic exclusions, while UnderwriteAI processes 1.2 million quotes daily at 95% STP, slashing manual reviews 40%. Combined with Guidewire cloud, expect 20% back-office cuts and 50bps annual expense compression, fueling profitable growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Credit Suisse. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera: Thanks. On premium growth guidance, how does the 10-12% for 2025 factor in potential rate softening?

Maria Gonzalez: Mike, the guide assumes 4-6% net rates, stable cats per RMS, low-teens new biz. Upside from telematics/cyber, risks offset by ML risk selection -150bps attritional LR. Segments like E&S/specialty accelerate to 12-14%, personal 8-10% on homeowners momentum.

Operator: Our final question from Sarah Wong with BlackRock.

Sarah Wong: Regarding reinsurance, any updates on expected recoveries and program costs for 2025?

Maria Gonzalez: Sarah, pipeline $1.8 billion firm, no loss creep assumed. Jan1 renewals blended trad/ILS/cat bonds at -5% cost despite hardening, reinst $400 million. APAC index expansions enhance efficiency, supporting mid-90s COR.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
